description: Change of use from of Class E (Office) to Class Sui Generis (Larger HMO) to provide 9 rooms involving erection of a part one, part two storey rear extension, alterations to fenestrations and provision of refuse and cycle store.
decision_conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date hereof.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

If during implementation of this development, contamination is encountered which has not previously been identified, the additional contamination shall be fully assessed and a specific contaminated land assessment and associated remedial strategy shall be submitted to and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the additional remediation works are carried out. The agreed strategy shall be implemented in full prior to completion of the development hereby approved. Reason: If contamination is discovered during the development this will need to be managed appropriately to the satisfaction of Kingston Council and the Environment Agency so that there are no remaining unacceptable risks to human health or the environment, to ensure potential land contamination risks to human health and the environment are appropriately managed, to comply with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018).

Prior to the first occupation of the development, the internal cycle storage facility for nine (9) bicycles shown on approved drawing No. 3 of 14 shall be fully installed and made available for use by residents. The cycle storage shall be kept secure, covered, and retained exclusively for cycle parking thereafter.  Reason: To encourage sustainable and active modes of transport, to comply with Policy 36 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018) and Policy T5 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the first occupation of the development, the communal refuse and recycling store located at the rear of the property (accessed via Queen's Road) shall be fully implemented in accordance with approved drawing No. 3 of 14, and shall be retained as such for use by occupants at all times.  Reason: To ensure proper waste management and protect streetscene aesthetics and local amenity, to comply with Policies 28 and 29 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018) and Policies SI 7 and SI 8 of the London Plan (2021).

The development shall operate at all times in strict accordance with the measures and operational procedures set out in the submitted HMO Management Plan (prepared by Cosy Hauz, July 2026), including tenant onboarding checks, waste management routines, anti-social behaviour policies, and emergency contact arrangements.  Reason: To ensure the property is responsibly managed to protect local residential amenity and prevent nuisance, to comply with Policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018).

Prior to the commencement of any above-ground works hereby permitted, a scheme for habitat creation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in the form of a Biodiversity Enhancement and Management Plan (BEMP). The BEMP shall provide:a) Details of the substrate-based biodiverse green roof (including plant species, depth, and cross-sections);b) A delivery timetable;c) A long-term monitoring and management schedule to maintain the habitat in perpetuity.The development shall be implemented strictly in accordance with the approved BEMP.  Reason: To ensure the development complies with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018) and Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021).

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Fire Safety Statement dated July 2026. Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with the Mayor's London Plan Policy D12.

The external appearance of the development hereby permitted shall be constructed in strict accordance with the materials and finishes specified in the approved External Material Schedule (including facing bricks, white render, concrete roof tiles, and uPVC fenestration). The approved materials shall be used in the construction of the development, completed prior to first occupation, and retained thereafter.  Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and preserve the character and appearance of the Holy Trinity Conservation Area, to comply with Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018) and Policy HC1 of the London Plan (2021).

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Statement dated 2 July 2027. Prior to first occupation,' 'as-built' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that the development has achieved the targeted reduction in CO2 emissions. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence.  Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The rating level of the noise from the plant hereby permitted shall be at least 5dBA lower than the existing background noise level at any given time of operation. The noise levels shall be measured or predicted 1m externally to any window at the nearest residential façade. Measurements and assessment shall be made according to British Standard 4142:2014.Reason: To safeguard the residential amenity of adjoining and nearby occupiers, to comply with Policies 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018).

Prior to the installation of any external plant (including the Air Source Heat Pump), an acoustic report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that the rating level of noise emitted from the plant will be at least 5 dBA lower than the existing background noise level at any given time of operation. The noise levels shall be measured or predicted 1 metre externally from any window at the nearest residential façade in accordance with BS 4142:2014. The plant shall be installed and maintained in strict accordance with the approved acoustic report.  Reason: To safeguard the residential amenity of adjoining and nearby occupiers, to comply with Policies 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018).
